identity.name: link_parcel_addresses
identity.description: Populates parcel_address_points, the spatial bridge table Phase 2d link-parcels.js Strategy 1a (0.97 confidence) and Phase 2e link-coa-to-parcels.js Tier 1a (0.95 confidence) both consume as their top-of-cascade address match: for every parcel with a non-NULL geom, ONE server-side INSERT...SELECT...JOIN ST_Within(address_point, parcel)...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING statement per keyset batch, no retraction, no primary/fallback split.

why_lock.text: Lock 115 is not the spec number (54) — spec 54's slot is already taken by load-address-points.js (lock 96), and spec 55's slot is taken by load-parcels.js. Free-range ID, registered in src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts LOCK_ID_REGISTRY. Kept textually per §5.4 so that registry stays green across the conversion.

guard_why.text: No column on this write target is ever updated after insert — computed_at is a write-once RUN_AT stamp, never revisited. A change guard would compare a row against itself and always pass; the genuine gap is retraction (LPA-D1), not a missing guard. Grandfathered in scripts/steps/_schema/grandfathered.json (Rule 9: an existing step must be able to declare its truth), keyed on write_discipline.guard, not .class.

guard_columns_why.text: LG-9 escape hatch. "all_declared" expands over computed_at, a columns[].source "run_at" column — normally banned (a run-clock column is DISTINCT FROM its stored value on every run, so guarding on it would rewrite every row every run). Moot here: guard is "none", so guard_columns is never consulted to build an IS DISTINCT FROM clause — there is no OTHER non-key column to name, since parcel_id/address_point_id are the key and computed_at is the only non-key column, which is exactly why the guard is genuinely "none" (guard_why above).

write_discipline.scope: unscoped INSERT — the batch loop re-scans the FULL parcels WHERE geom IS NOT NULL population every run (LPA-D2: idempotent via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, not resumable — no batch-position checkpoint is persisted), filtered per-batch by id > lastId

why.text: LG-18 (this pilot). LPA-D1: the W3 retraction breach is a genuine DEFECT (a parcel/address-point geom correction can silently invalidate an already-written row, and nothing here ever re-evaluates or removes it) with ZERO measured live exposure today (0 of 511,224 rows fail ST_Within, this session). Per Spec 123 §3.1: pin the non-retraction as-is, convert, prove bit-identical output, decide the fix as a separate ruling — not bundled into this conversion commit. retract:"none" below is the truthful, pinned declaration; parcel_address_points_stale_st_within_count (checks[]) makes the live exposure OBSERVABLE every run so the pin is never silent.

One write target, one write statement per batch — the single INSERT...SELECT...JOIN ST_Within...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (LG-18's executeInsertSelectNoRetract), repeated once per keyset-paginated batch (measured ~487 batches at BATCH_SIZE 1000 over 486,530 parcels).

The GIST index the batch join's ST_Within(ap.geom, pb.geom) predicate seeks on the parcel side. Without it every batch degrades to a sequential scan — the same class of failure tasks/lessons.md records for link_massing's spatial GiST indexes.
The GIST index (migration 162) the batch join seeks on the address_points side. Without it the join is unbounded on a 525,346-row table.
Measured live: relrowsecurity=true, 0 policies. Under any role that does not bypass RLS the INSERT affects 0 rows with NO error — indistinguishable from an unchanged corpus.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a value the library already measured — a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition. It must redden the run, not drop its row.

why.text: T4 (Fold B, Cross-read Adversary AMEND, 2026-08-29) — replaces the DROPPED 5-id allow-list Fold A first proposed (the 5 named ids were merely top-5 of a 4,296-parcel non-CONDO tail with no measured discontinuity vs ranks 6-10, and "registered as COMMON" was uncorroborated). Default 20 — measured live 130 non-CONDO parcels exceed it TODAY, which fires this WARN by construction. R-H (Spec 124 Rule 10 addendum): a metric expected to be permanently non-zero is WARN with a declared, machine-observable retighten condition, never FAIL, never silently PASSed by an allow-list. RETIGHTEN CONDITION: if the count materially drops from 130 without any code change (a parcel-boundary correction, not a threshold edit), review lowering the default toward the observed floor. LPA-D3 (peel 8b, 2026-08-29): the limit form is `viol <= 0`, NOT `viol == 0` — `verdict.js`'s VIOL_RE distinguishes the two on purpose (`== ` is exact-match, for a literal `viol == 0` with no `limit_from_config`; `<=` is a ceiling, for a config-substituted bound) and `resolveLimit` substitutes the config value onto WHATEVER comparator is declared — `== 0` written for a `limit_from_config` bound silently becomes `== <threshold>`, an exact-equality check a fluctuating count almost never satisfies, not a ceiling.

expect.of: CONDO parcels whose linked-address-point fan-out exceeds the declared per-parcel ceiling

why.text: T5 (Fold B). A large condo complex's common-elements parcel legitimately contains many unit entrances (measured live max 346, ~26.6-acre parcel 469748, address_number range 1-98 — plausible per this pilot's Reality-Check pass). Default 400, comfortably above the measured p99 (80) and max (346) — fires only on a genuine outlier, unlike T4's standing-population shape. LPA-D3 (peel 8b, 2026-08-29): `viol <= 0`, not `viol == 0` — see T4's `why` for the shared root cause (`verdict.js`'s VIOL_RE `==`-vs-`<=` distinction, silently broken by a `limit_from_config` bound authored with `== 0`). Measured live before this fix: EVERY real run since commit 7 reported this check WARN (0 violations against a 400 ceiling, `0 == 400` is false), including peel 8a's forced capture — a false WARN the whole pilot, never a FAIL/blocking gate so it never broke anything, but it silently misrepresented a genuinely clean CONDO population as an outlier every single run.

why.text: LPA-D1 — the W3 retraction breach, PINNED per Spec 123 §3.1. A parcel boundary correction or address-point coordinate correction can silently invalidate an already-written row, and this step has NO mechanism that ever re-evaluates or removes it (0 DELETE anywhere). Measured live exposure TODAY: 0 of 511,224 rows. INFO (not WARN/FAIL) — this is a structural fact to surface every run (Rule 1: nothing hidden), never a threshold to gate on until a separate ruling decides to build the retraction mechanism.

deviations.from: the pre-conversion script's own header comment (:32-34, 'Resumable: each batch commits independently; operator Ctrl-C leaves the DB in a consistent partial state and a re-run picks up where we left off.')

why.text: LPA-D2 (2026-08-29). Measured: lastParcelId was a LOCAL variable, initialized to -1, never persisted to any table or file (:148) — every invocation, including one immediately after a Ctrl-C, restarts the batch loop from id > -1, i.e. the FULL parcel population. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes this idempotent (safe: no duplicate rows) but it is NOT resumable in the claimed sense (efficient re-entry, skipping already-completed batches). The code was already correct-and-safe; only the header's PROSE claimed a capability the code never had. Corrected here and in link-parcel-addresses.notes.json's read_this_way block — the code itself needed no behavior change.

deviations.adjudicated_by: measured this pilot (§1 PH-0 boundary freeze / §2 PH-3 intent ledger, finding 2), 2026-08-29

limitations.what: LPA-D1: the W3 retraction breach. parcel_address_points guarantees the AP geom is inside the parcel AT WRITE TIME (link-parcels.js:282's own in-file comment states the reliance), but a later upstream geom edit (load-parcels.js / load-address-points.js both UPDATE geom on ON CONFLICT for an existing row) can make that stale with ZERO mechanism to detect or repair it. PINNED per Spec 123 §3.1 — convert first, decide the retraction fix as a separate ruling.
limitations.measured: 0 of 511,224 rows fail ST_Within(ap.geom, p.geom) today (2026-08-29 session)

limitations.what: computed_at is a SINGLE timestamp shared across all 511,224 rows written by the origin run, not a per-row per-invocation audit trail — a future reset/rebuild mechanism must not rely on computed_at to distinguish rows by run.
limitations.measured: 1 distinct computed_at value across the live table (Fold A, Reality-Check note, 2026-08-29)

recovery.reset: No TRUNCATE/rebuild mechanism exists. A re-run (LINK_PARCEL_ADDRESSES_FORCE_FULL=1 bypasses the ledger gate) re-scans the full parcels population from id > -1; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes this idempotent, which is the only available reset today — declare-only per the A-1 ruling, no destructive rebuild path built this pilot.

interrupted_why.text: No destructive retraction target exists on this step (class D, retract:"none", LPA-D1 pinned) — there is nothing for an interrupted run to leave half-retracted. R-F item 1 (2026-08-29): this pilot does NOT itself exercise or close R-B's crashed/stuck-running reader gap; it stays carried forward to whichever future pilot first ships a genuine retract_when:"full_only" target.

before_image_why.text: R-M / LG-17's before-image mechanism applies to a destructive retraction; this step has none (class D, retract:"none"). Each batch's INSERT is additive and reversible-by-DELETE-of-the-batch's-own-new-rows if ever needed, which is not the same hazard class a before-image protects against.
